evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'I'll be needing ten to fifteen minutes of your time to ask you a few questions regarding the move' but did not frame it as a promise of a dependable quote and did not wait for explicit customer confirmation ('Does that sound good?') before continuing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'if you have any concerns about the moving process aside from the pricing or maybe any worries or any answers that you'd like' — asked before logistics probing started.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised no concerns (said 'No, not at all I don't have a ton of stuff'), so N/A.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Customer raised no concerns, so N/A.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covered property type (1 bed apartment, 850 sqft), floor/stories (14th floor), elevator access (yes, reservable), distance from elevator to truck (50 feet), distance from elevator to unit (one unit away), special considerations (king bed, marble-top dresser, TV ~60 inches), destination property type (1 story house), destination access (driveway, 4 front steps). All seven categories touched.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep did NOT offer packing services. Customer asked about wardrobe boxes and rep said 'you have to load into those boxes since you are not availing the packing services' — rep acknowledged the lack of packing but never offered it as an option.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked 'Normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?' — asked and answered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep said 'for a one bedroom apartment we finish the move-in. Three and a half hours but in your case we're coming from a high floor from the fourteenth floor though the elevator is reserved, I'm still gonna add a buffer into that... So for this move I estimate this to finish in three and a half to four and a half hours with two movers and one truck.' Range given, personalized to high floor and elevator buffer.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed $105/hour per mover ($210 total), $75 travel fee one-time, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, all-inclusive language ('everything is included, gas and truck taxes, insurance...') — full framing present. Rep also said 'this is only my estimate. So, if ever the move will take less than this, you will only be charged for how much time we used' (not a guess framing).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Rep moved straight to 'So, I can schedule your move-in the morning of Sunday. 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM is the arrival window. Are you okay with that timeframe?' — skipped the feels-fair check entirely.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not deliver or close the loop on either of the Two Promises.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent. Rep proceeded directly to logistics confirmation (unit number, confirmation email).
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable variant. Rep scheduled the move and confirmed details without an explicit booking ask.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details across all seven categories (property type, floors, distances, special items, destination access) with natural follow-up probing, creating a detailed and accurate move profile.
coaching_note: Rep skipped the entire Section 5 (Two Promises), never asked Section 4's 'Does that feel fair?' check, and moved into booking without an explicit Section 7 ask for the business — this is an incomplete close that left value (guarantees/coverage) undelivered and the customer's commitment unclear.
